messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime-streaming.p99 has breached SLO in production cluster us-east-1. p95=420ms (SLO 250ms), p99=2.8s (SLO 1s). Triggered at 13:02 UTC. Paging on-call.

carmen: acknowleged, taking primary. :raised_hand: first pass: is this across all models or specific to streaming endpoints?

mike: seeing large tail on streaming for model:redwood-llama-13b-quant since the rollout ~12:45 UTC. Non-streaming endpoints look mostly normal. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/d/streaming?panel=latency (linked)

sara: looks like KV cache misses spiked after the quantized model variant landed on the pool. eviction rate shot up, and I see many cold prefix fetches. Might be global cache key schema change.

josh: customer impact: two enterprise customers reported UI stalls; sessions drop after a few tokens. Not widespread but high severity for streaming use-cases.

ellie: quick checks I've run: node CPU and GPU util steady, but worker process async queue length increased and streams stayed open longer. Also observed many 504s from stream-proxy logs:

```
[13:03:12] stream-proxy: stream_id=xyz state=stall last_msg=token_chunk timeout=30007ms
[13:03:13] kv-cache: miss key=prefix:abcd
[13:03:14] model-host: warn decode_latency=2100ms
```

ops-bot: Paging notes: PagerDuty incident PDID-8743 created and notified on-call-sre. Incident channel pinned.

carmen: initial mitigation plan: 1) throttle new model rollout (stop further placements) 2) route streaming traffic to fallback variant (non-quantized) 3) attempt cache warm-up for hot prefixes. Who can flip routes?

mike: I can flip routing in ~2 mins. Requesting a quick rollback if fallback doesn't restore latency. Also propose temporarily increasing streaming chunk size to reduce round trips (streaming_chunk_ms -> 80ms from 20ms).

sara: cache warm-up: I can prefetch top 200 prefixes from production metrics into prefix-cache, but need a couple minutes for safe population. Also adding a short TTL increase to reduce churn.

josh: We should communicate to affected customers with a short note: "We detected streaming stalls, working on hotfix; some sessions may experience delays." I'll draft.

ellie: I'll run a tail of streaming-worker logs and confirm whether stalls correlate with specific host IDs. Command: `kubectl logs -f deploy/stream-worker -c worker --since=5m | grep stall`

mike: routing flipped to fallback model variant (redwood-llama-13b-fp16) for streaming route. :white_check_mark: Monitor p95/p99 now.

sara: kicked off cache prefetch job for top prefixes. Also bumping prefix-cache TTL to 60s.

carmen: monitoring dashboard: p95 dropped to 240ms within 90s of routing flip, p99 now 980ms. Still seeing a few stragglers in the tail.

mike: temporary config change: `streaming_chunk_ms=80` applied to stream-proxy group a, propagating. Might increase token throughput but reduce number of network hops.

ellie: after config change, logs show fewer `stream-proxy: stall` entries. No new 504s in last 30s.

ops-bot: PD incident updated: status -> "mitigated" by cabot. Auto-notify customers: disabled.

josh: Sent customer note to affected accounts. cc: AE / CSM.

carmen: summary so far for the incident timeline: root cause appears to be higher-than-expected KV cache churn introduced by the quantized variant alongside many small streaming chunks causing more round trips; combined led to cold-prefix stalls. Mitigations: routing to fp16 fallback, cache warm-up + TTL bump, increase streaming_chunk_ms. Latency back within SLOs for now.

sara: action items: 1) rollback rollout of quantized model until we fix cache key compatibility and warm startup; 2) add automated prefix warm-up step to deployment pipeline; 3) add an alert on kv-cache-eviction-rate to prevent recurrence.

mike: going to open a short RFC for rollout gating and an infra job to validate prefix-key stability. I'll also run a synthetic streaming load test against quantized variant once fixed.

ellie: collecting logs and trace ids for postmortem. Please add any customer-reported timestamps to the thread.

carmen: handing off to post-incident owner @mike for follow-ups and to coordinate postmortem. Closing live triage. :slightly_smiling_face:

incident-bot: Incident PDID-8743 status changed to RESOLVED at 13:12 UTC. For follow-up, file a postmortem and link to this thread.
